capsuleTopic.title: Temptation of Jesus
capsuleTopic.subtitle: Spirit · wilderness · Son · Scripture · worship · testing
capsuleTopic.orientation: Enter the wilderness encounter through Matthew, Mark, and Luke as distinct witnesses. Earlier Scripture supplies the words and patterns they name; baptism and sonship set the immediate context; later tests and letters show how temptation language continues.
capsuleTopic.trailPrompt: Follow the Spirit, wilderness, hunger, sonship, Scripture, worship, protection, departure, and later pressure without blending the witnesses or turning every biblical test into this Event.

passages.excerpt: He came out and went, as his custom was, to the Mount of Olives. His disciples also followed him. When he was at the place, he said to them, “Pray that you don’t enter into temptation.”…
passages.observation: At the Mount of Olives Jesus tells the disciples to pray against entering temptation, prays about the cup and the Father’s will, and finds them sleeping from sorrow.

passages.title: Paul reads Israel’s wilderness as warning and encouragement
passages.excerpt: Now I would not have you ignorant, brothers, that our fathers were all under the cloud, and all passed through the sea; and were all baptized into Moses in the cloud and in the sea; and…
passages.observation: Paul recalls cloud, sea, food, drink, desire, idolatry, testing, and grumbling. He warns the community and says temptation is common and God provides a way through.

passages.title: Suffering under temptation becomes grounds for help
passages.excerpt: Since then the children have shared in flesh and blood, he also himself in the same way partook of the same, that through death he might bring to nothing him who had the power of death,…
passages.observation: Hebrews speaks of shared flesh and blood, death, the devil, release from fear, Abraham’s offspring, priestly mercy, atonement, suffering, temptation, and help.

passages.title: The great high priest was tempted yet without sin
passages.excerpt: Having then a great high priest who has passed through the heavens, Jesus, the Son of God, let’s hold tightly to our confession. For we don’t have a high priest who can’t be touched wit…
passages.observation: Hebrews names Jesus as the Son of God and great high priest, says he shares the feeling of human weakness and was tempted in every way without sin, then invites approach for mercy and help.

passages.title: James separates God from the source of temptation
passages.excerpt: Blessed is a person who endures temptation, for when he has been approved, he will receive the crown of life which the Lord promised to those who love him. Let no man say when he is tem…
passages.observation: James blesses endurance under trial, says God tempts no one, traces temptation through one’s own desire, and contrasts desire’s path with God’s good gifts and new birth.
